{{Short description|Maximal abelian extension of an algebraic number field}}
In [[algebraic number theory]], the '''genus field''' <math>\Gamma(K)</math> of an [[algebraic number field]] <math>K</math> is the [[Maximal element|maximal]] [[abelian extension]] of <math>K</math> which is obtained by composing an absolutely abelian field with <math>K</math> and which is  [[unramified]] at all finite primes of <math>K</math>.  The '''genus number''' of <math>K</math> is the degree <math>[\Gamma(K):K]</math> and the '''genus group''' is the [[Galois group]] of <math>\Gamma(K)</math> over <math>K</math>.

If <math>K</math> is itself absolutely abelian, the genus field may be described as the maximal absolutely abelian extension of <math>K</math> unramified at all finite primes: this definition was used by Leopoldt and Hasse.

If <math>K=\Q(\sqrt{m})</math> (<math>m</math> square-free) is a quadratic field of discriminant <math>D</math>, the genus field of <math>K</math> is a composite of quadratic fields.  Let ''p''<sub>''i''</sub> run over the prime factors of <math>D</math>.  For each such prime ''p'', define ''p''<sup>&lowast;</sup> as follows:

:<math> p^* = \pm p \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \text{ if } p \text{ is odd} ; </math>
:<math> 2^* = -4, 8, -8 \text{ according as } m \equiv 3 \pmod 4, 2 \pmod 8, -2 \pmod 8 . </math>

Then the genus field is the composite <math>K(\sqrt{p_i^*}).</math>
